newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Euromark volatility eases after rally.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Euromark volatility eases after rally.

text.p: Implied volatility of Euromark options traded on LIFFE eased back on Thursday after the recent Bund-inspired rise, traders said.
Declines in the German Bund futures market, where the June contract has lost about two points since the start of the week, added upward pressure to Euromark volatility.
"Vol spiked up with the weakness in Bunds, but has started going down again," said a trader at a French brokerage in London. "It still has some way to go."
June Euromark futures were unchanged at 96.68 by 1400 GMT, while September was up 0.01 at 96.58.
June Bund futures were down 0.16 at 99.79.

June options vol slid to 10.3 percent, from 10.5 percent earlier in the day. September was at 13.5, compared with 13.7 earlier, and December was down 0.2 at 15.6 percent. So-called "red March", March 1998, was also down slightly at 17.6 percent.
Traders said there was also some selling of volatility ahead of the weekend, keeping in mind that the coming week will be abbreviated for much of Europe as Easter holidays start.
There were three major trades noted in the Euromark options, with calls dominating activity, according to a trader at a German bank in London.
A December one-by-two call spread was done at the 96.75/97 even strikes. The trade involved buying one lot of the 96.75 and selling two of the 97.00.
A calendar spread was traded in June, where the 96.75 calls were bought and the 97.00 calls were sold. This was done 2,000 times.
An outright buy of 97.00 calls was noted at the 97.00 December strike. More than 4,000 contracts had traded at this strike by 1400 GMT.
